newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: U.S.-Australia wargames affected by cyclone.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Australia wargames affected by cyclone.

text.p: A cyclone causing strong winds and high waves along Australia's northeast coast forced Australian and U.S. authorities on Monday to scale down their biggest wargames since World War Two, a spokesman said.
"We have had to make some modifications to the exercise," U.S. Major Ben Owens told Reuters.
Tropical Cyclone Justin is causing wind gusts up to 170 kph (105 mph) and waves up to five metres (15 feet) around Australia's Great Barrier Reef, where operation Tandem Thrust started on Monday.

Tandem Thrust, a U.S.-led land, sea and air exercise involving 27,000 personnel and more than 200 warships, is the most visible sign of closer defence ties between Canberra and Washington since Australia's conservative government came to power a year ago.

Owens said an aircraft carrier battlegroup and an amphibious assault group had been ordered to stand off outside the reef area for safety and to minimise the risk of environmental damage in case of an accident.
The bad weather has forced some parts of the exercise to be cancelled and others delayed, he said. But most land exercises were proceeding on schedule.

Cyclone Justin, about 1,000 kms (600 miles) wide, was expected to hit the Queensland state coast on Wednesday, the Bureau of Meteorology said on Monday. On Monday it was almost stationary about 580 kms (360 miles) off the resort of Cairns.
But Justin was not expected to reach the intensity of previous cyclones that have devastated coastal communities in Australia, bureau forecaster Jeffrey Crane said.
Although it is larger, Justin lacked the "punch" of cyclone Tracy, which killed at least 65 people in 1974 when it ripped through Darwin in Australia's Northern Territory, Crane said.
